documentation: docs/MCU_MAPPING.md - section 4 defines this file (layer 3, the binding table), section 2 defines the MIDI numbers (layer 1), and section 2.7 records the hardware verification named below. Read by prism_surface::Bindings::load (S22), which is given the text rather than a path: a profile that will not parse answers with the built-in defaults and a warning, and can never block startup. The bindings below reproduce those built-in defaults exactly, and a test asserts it - so editing this file is how the defaults are changed, and deleting it changes nothing.
notOurNoteMap: The note and CC numbers are deliberately NOT in this file. They live in exactly one place, prism_surface::profile::X_TOUCH, because a second copy of a 104-row table is a second thing to keep in step - which is what holding it in one constant was for. This file maps logical controls to commands.

measured.deviceReady: F0 00 00 66 14 01 <7 ascii serial> <4 ascii challenge> F7

untested.footSwitches: Notes 102 and 103 need a pedal in the FOOT SW jacks; nothing was plugged in. Neither note has an LED, which is expected of a jack.
untested.cablePull: S21 built the handling and asserts it against a mock: the port going away invalidates the shadow model, stops all traffic, tells the engine nothing, and a reconnect redraws the whole surface once, paced. What is untested is whether a real unplug and replug produces exactly one Disconnected and one connected from the MIDI backend S22 chooses - a question about that backend, not about prism-surface.

verification.knownFault: Saturating both directions at once - a burst of large SysEx writes while replies are outstanding - loses messages and can stop the surface transmitting entirely while it goes on receiving normally. Only a power cycle recovers it. Pace the outbound path (30 Hz, coalesced, minimum gap) and never poll the handshake. docs/MCU_MAPPING.md section 2.7.

sharedMode.summary: This surface is to be run in the X-Touch's combined Xctl+MC mode, driving the venue's sound console over Xctl and PrismDMX over MC at the same time. docs/MCU_MAPPING.md section 4.3.
sharedMode.provenance: Stated by the operator who owns and runs the desk. NOT measured in S20, which verified plain MC mode. Verifying it needs the sound console present.
sharedMode.authority: S21 holds this same set as McuProfile::permanent, in code, because the shadow model consults it every frame. THAT is the authoritative copy; the list below is this file's description of the deployment. If they ever disagree, the constant wins and this file is wrong.
sharedMode.consequence: Everything else - strips, faders, encoders, F-keys, bank and channel buttons - follows the operator's switch between the two hosts. Nothing is unreachable: SMPTE/Beats gives PrismDMX the whole surface at any time. What the permanent set buys is that it needs NO switch, which is what matters during a show.
sharedMode.designGoal: The transport section is the always-hot part of the console, so spend it on live-show work - free assignments included, such as a tap for speed against a particular speed master, a macro, or a look. It is explicitly NOT a requirement that everything important fit into five buttons. The bindings below are a reasonable starting point, not a layout.
sharedMode.feedbackRule: The shadow model may only drive LEDs for controls MC currently holds. Lighting a strip LED while the surface is showing the sound console is ignored at best, and fights that console's own feedback at worst.

reserved.reason: In the combined Xctl+MC mode this button switches the surface between the two hosts. It is the operator's way back to the sound desk, so PrismDMX never binds it - in ANY mode, so that one profile is safe on a desk whose mode nobody has checked. It also has no LED (measured, S20).
No LED on this device (measured, S20). Bindable in principle, but a control with no feedback is a poor place for an operating function, so the default profile leaves it alone.

bindingNotes: Each action's 't' is a prism_surface::SurfaceAction variant, which resolves to exactly one prism_domain::Command. The arguments a command needs but a binding cannot know - executor_id, level, view_id, the attribute under the jog wheel - are supplied by layer 3 from the control's own value and a SurfaceContext the daemon fills in from the session (D7: executorPage * 8 + strip index). 'Strip[*]' is one entry rather than eight: a fader bank has one binding per row, and the strip index is what picks the executor. A control listed with a null action is deliberately left alone, which is not the same as one this file forgot.
controlNames: Strip[*].Fader, Strip[*].Encoder, Strip[*].Button.{Rec,Solo,Mute,Select,VPotPush}, Main.Fader, Global.Jog, and Global.<button> for each of the 64 panel buttons named by prism_surface::GlobalButton. A control this list does not name is refused, and so is a control bound twice.
additionsToSection41: Strip[*].Button.VPotPush is not a section 4.1 row. It selects that strip's executor, because the transport section, the Flip button and the main fader all act on the SELECTED executor and the selection has to be reachable from the surface.
Global.Enter -> Redo is not a section 4.1 row either. Undo without a redo beside it is a desk with half an Oops.
deviationsClosedInS34: Main fader: section 4.1 calls it XFade of the selected executor. The binding is still ExecutorMaster on the selected executor - there is one fader command for all four ExecutorFaderFunctions - but prism-core now routes it through the executor's own faderFunction, so a fader set to XFade crossfades and the row means what it says.
Play: section 4.1 gives it On. Command::ExecutorButton now carries a function, so Play sends On and Stop sends Off rather than both resolving to the nearest command that existed.

Strip Rec/Solo/Mute/Select: the binding is now the button POSITION (Slot 0-3) and the executor's own buttonFunctions decide what it does - which is what section 4.1's configurable column always meant. All eight functions are reachable, including Flash, Toggle and LearnSpeed.
carriedForward: A tap for speed has a target now: ExecutorButtonFunction::LearnSpeed on a strip button, or bound outright on a transport key as { t: Function, function: LearnSpeed }. Two taps inside four seconds mean the running cue's transition should take that long. What it does NOT have yet is a speed master separate from the executor - Executor::speed is per executor, which is what the domain carries.

The transport section and the jog wheel are the controls that reach PrismDMX without a mode switch (see sharedMode). Their bindings above are a reasonable starting point, not a layout: they are the five keys worth spending on live-show work.

D7 (executor paging on Faderbank) and D8 (SelectView on Channel) sit outside the permanent set, so in shared operation they cost a switch to the full surface. Acceptable for setup-shaped work, and a reason not to put anything time-critical there.

The Encoder Assign section has six buttons and docs/MCU_MAPPING.md section 4.1 names five feature groups. AssignInstrument is left unbound rather than doubled up: a button that repeats its neighbour teaches an operator that it is broken.
